question: Who was the author of the famous work ‘Shishupala Vadha’ ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Magha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Magha was a classical Sanskrit poet who flourished in the 7th century.

• His most famous work is 'Shishupala Vadha', an epic poem based on the Mahabharata.

• 'Shishupala Vadha' is known for its complex wordplay, ornate poetry, and intricate descriptions.

• The work is considered one of the five great epics of classical Sanskrit literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Shishupala Vadha**

• 'Shishupala Vadha' translates to "The Slaying of Shishupala" and is an epic poem composed by Magha in the 7th century AD.

• The poem is composed in 20 sargas (cantos) and contains approximately 1,800 verses.

• It narrates the story of Shishupala, a king who was an enemy of Krishna, and how Krishna eventually slays him.

• The work is highly regarded for its literary style, including its use of elaborate metaphors and similes, and the complexity of its poetic techniques.

• **Sanskrit Literature**

• Sanskrit literature is one of the richest and oldest literatures in the world, with a history spanning over 3,000 years.

• It includes a wide range of genres such as epic poetry, drama, philosophy, religious texts, and scientific treatises.

• Some of the most well-known works in Sanskrit literature include the Vedas, the Upanishads, the Mahabharata, the Ramayana, and the works of Kalidasa.

• Sanskrit has also influenced many other Indian languages and literatures over the centuries.

• **Other Classical Sanskrit Poets**

• **Jayadeva:** Known for his work 'Gita Govinda', which describes the love between Krishna and Radha.

• **Bhatti:** Renowned for his work 'Bhattikavya' (Ravanavadha), which is a poetic masterpiece known for its linguistic and grammatical complexity.

• **Bharavi:** Famous for his epic poem 'Kiratarjuniya', which depicts an episode from the Mahabharata where Arjuna is blessed by Lord Shiva.
